aboutMe.title: Data Scientist | Natural Hazard & Risk Analyst | Scientific Computing
aboutMe.description: Building reproducible analytical workflows and translating complex datasets into actionable insights.

story.heading: Curiosity is the whole job
paragraphs: Hi, I'm Mingshen. I'm a research data scientist, and I make things on YouTube and a podcast.

I live in Potsdam, Germany. For the past few years my work has been about earthquakes and natural hazards — using data to understand things that are hard to predict, and then explaining what came out of it to people who are not specialists.
If I had to put the work in one line: use data to understand risk, and say it in language anyone can follow.

story.heading: Travel, books, films, and overthinking
paragraphs: Six years into living abroad, I still love travelling, reading, watching films, and turning life's small questions over far longer than they need.
Since 2023 I have been putting those observations into videos and episodes — a YouTube channel, and a podcast called Huh? Germany! about what living here is actually like.

experience.title: Research Data Scientist
descriptions: Coordinated with international teams in EU-funded projects and communicated results to scientific and non-specialist audiences.
Developed and maintained reproducible Python-based scientific workflows for geospatial and time-series data analysis.

experience.title: Research Data Analyst
descriptions: Modelled seismic time-series data for seismic hazard assessments and validated results against empirical datasets to identify behavioural patterns.
Produced analytical reports comparing modelled seismic outputs to empirical data for government risk planning.

education.description: EU Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellow. Graduated magna cum laude.
